title: Candidate Rehearsal to Onboard Continuity Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight playbook for running a candidate-facing rehearsal session that doubles as a structured handoff to hiring managers and the onboarding plan. Goal is to reduce first-week friction, preserve interview context (signals + unstructured notes), and proactively surface ramp risks.

Scope / When to use:
- Use for senior IC and manager-level hires where cross-functional handoff is required (eng, product, design).
- Optional for mid-level roles if hiring time-to-productivity is critical.
- Not required for contractor/short-term roles unless specified in req.

Quick TL;DR checklist (one-pager for recruiter):
[ ] Confirm candidate ok with 60–75 minute rehearsal session (recording optional).
[ ] Send 3 bullet prep list + company/team context doc 48h ahead.
[ ] Book hiring manager + two interview panelists for 30 min post-rehearsal sync.
[ ] Prepare onboarding-access checklist and send to infra ops pre-approve.

Pre-rehearsal (owner: recruiter, t-minus 72–48h):
- Share 2-pager: team mission, current roadmap bullets, recent production metrics (top-level).
- Confirm rubric to be used in interview + scoring scale (1–5 anchors). Link: confluence:HR/Interview-Guides-2025
- Create a short candidate context summary: source, compensation band, relocation/remote status, notice period, known constraints.
- Invite candidate to rehearsal with explicit agenda: technical problem simulation (30m), culture/leadership Q&A (15m), role expectations (15m).

Rehearsal agenda (approx 60–75m):
- 5m: quick intros + session framing (recruiter)
- 30m: simulated on-call / design or coding prompt (use interview prompt library id: PEOPLEOPS-482-A)
  - Focus on thinking aloud and tradeoffs; panelists play stakeholder roles.
- 15m: behavioral + leadership scenarios (STAR prompts)
- 10m: role expectations and ramp conversation with hiring manager
- 5m: next steps and candidate questions

Panel choreography notes (for panel lead):
- Panel should explicitly mark the start/stop of candidate thinking time.
- Avoid multiple interruptions in the first 8 minutes of a problem.
- Use the rubric anchors for each dimension: problem solving, technical breadth, systems thinking, communication, teamwork.
- Capture 2–3 explicit examples to justify any 4 or 5 scores.

Scoring normalization quick guide (to use in post-rehearsal sync):
- Each interviewer records: score per dimension (1–5) + 1-line justification + uncertainty flag (low/medium/high).
- During sync, surface any >1 point variance in a dimension; ask for an evidence example.
- If variance persists, default to hiring manager tie-break after cross-check with recruiting lead.

Candidate deliverables from rehearsal (what we send back to hiring manager):
- One-paragraph candidate summary (recruiter)
- Panel rubric consolidated (spreadsheet row)
- Short list of ramp concerns and suggested 30/60/90 goals draft
- Recording or transcript (if candidate consents) and timestamped notable moments

Onboarding continuity handoff (immediately after offer accepted)
- Owner: recruiter -> handoff to hiring manager + people ops ops lead
- Handoff packet includes: candidate summary, consolidated rubric, prioritized ramp risks, equipment and access checklist, required trainings, mentor assignment suggestion.

First-week checklist (engineer example):
[ ] Laptop imaged with base image (tag: eng-base-2025)
[ ] VPN + SSO access provisioned
[ ] Slack + calendar invites + team channel added
[ ] 30/60/90 goals doc created and shared
[ ] Buddy assigned and intro email scheduled
[ ] Schedule: day1 orientation, day2 system deep-dive, day3 small onboarding ticket assigned

First-30/60/90 template (to adapt per role):
- 30d: Setup + visibility: complete dev environment, ship a non-critical change, meet cross-functional partners, complete security + compliance training
- 60d: Ownership: take lead on a small feature, run a postmortem, start mentoring rotations
- 90d: Impact: own a measurable feature, present results to team, propose a small roadmap improvement

Risk register (things to call out during rehersal/handoff):
- Candidate constrained by non-compete or long notice period -> affects start date and priority of first milestones
- Lack of domain experience (list areas) -> add shadowing and reading list
- Relocation support needed -> ramp expectations may slip

Notes to self / recruiter tips (informal):
- Use rehearsal as a chance to test real job-scenarios, not trick puzzles. We want signal on how they will operate on day1.
- Keep documentation lightweight: single sheet summary is most-read by hiring managers.
- Candidate mental load: explicitly say session is a rehearsal; reduce pressure by framing as collaborative.
- If candidate declines recording, ask permission for short note-only summary instead.

Open questions / TODOs for playbook iteration:
- Add a short template for design/PM hires (behavioral vs. portfolio split).
- Measure post-onboard time-to-first-PR for hires that had rehearsals vs those that didn’t. (tracking JIRA tag: onboarding-rehearsal)
- Decide standard retention of recordings (privacy/legal).

Next steps (owner: people-ops):
1) Pilot with 4 hires this quarter; collect feedback via 7-day pulse from hiring manager and new hire.
2) Iterate rubric anchors to remove ambiguous language (owners: María + Priya).
3) Build a short Confluence template and link from JD and interview invites.

Appendix: Manager handoff email template (one-paragraph + attachments)
Subject: New hire handoff — [Candidate name] (Start: YYYY-MM-DD)
Body: Quick snapshot attached (1p): background, consolidated rubric, top 3 ramp risks, proposed mentor. Please review and confirm equipment and access by [date].

--end of doc--
